project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to upgrade the heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) system and portions of the electrical system that support the HVAC in Columbia Lutheran Charities dba Columbia Memorial Hospital, in Astoria, Oregon. This 25-bed critical care facility serves the rural populations of Clatsop County, Oregon and portions of Pacific County, Washington. The current facility was built in 1977 and the existing HVAC system is outdated and does not provide the level of control or efficiency needed to meet the needs of a major incident involving air-born contaminants such as COVID-19. Since medical staff and patients will be accessing these portions of the facility, it is necessary to bring the HVAC system to current standards to minimize impacts from future pandemics similar to the current pandemic. In addition, the project includes new cold storage to increase vaccine storage capabilities. The new vaccine storage will be located in the same buildings benefiting from the funded HVAC upgrades. Overall, this project will ensure that this vital facility in the heart of the small, rural town of Astoria, Oregon and surrounding counties continues to provide critical services for years to come.

The existing facility was built in 2010 and is in good condition, however, increased demand for services resulting from the impacts of the pandemic have made it necessary to increase both dry and cold food storage capacity. funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) ECWAG - APPROPRIATED $1,000,000 LIMIT
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide spring box reconstruction, modifications to existing backwash ponds, the addition of a new chlorine feed system and the addition of new filters to the water treatment building. Site work will also include excavation and backfill of gravel and topsoil. Five spring boxes currently supply drinking water for the utility, however, two of the five boxes are damaged and not in use. One well and one water treatment plant are also not currently in use. In addition to the spring, the OWWSA has a well that was drilled in 1992 that houses an aging and non-functioning filtration system. A localized landslide event in 2020 damaged the spring boxes and caused water to stop flowing to the springs. Also, in 2020, a drought emergency was declared in the area due to unusually low water supplies and hot, dry conditions. The drought reduced flows in the OWWSA springs and the conditions carried over into 2021. These two events resulted in a significant decline in water quantity and quality. Overall, this project will ensure that this small, rural water authority will have the needed funds for upgrades which will ensure their ability to provide safe, potable water to the surrounding community for years to come.

naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to support a food bank. Brookings Harbor Community Helpers, headquartered in Brookings, Oregon has been operating in Curry County since 1984. Funds will be used to support increased staffing including the hiring of a bilingual interpreter and advocate to bridge the gap with the Hispanic Community. Due to the on-going need in the community, the applicant has had to purchase additional storage solutions to store and provide emergency COVID-19 supplies and bulk food supplies. Food purchases are rising due to reduced supply from the regional food bank and the addition of a Senior Fresh Food program that provides fresh vegetables to qualifying seniors. Ultimately this program will improve food security and access to nutritional options as the pandemic evolves. The increased client traffic to the Food Bank & Help Center has increased the need for food, PPEs, vaccines, vaccine event information, COVID-19 education and other health related services. Brookings Harbor Community Helpers continues to see increases in the clientele served and their needs and the associated expenses that are projected over the next 36 months to serve the community. Overall, this project will ensure that this rural area will have the needed funds to support the community and address the effects of the pandemic for years to come.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to assist with expenses related to the installation of equipment to divert contaminated storm water and replace damaged intake infrastructure. This will include replacing two pumps, the intake screens, and the installation of a steel flow diversion structure to direct debris away from the intake equipment. The water treatment plant was built in 1981 and is located on the Rogue River, downstream from multiple creek convergences that were affected by the September 2020 Labor Day wildfires, Alameda and South Obenchain. Extensive damage across these sub-watersheds and increased sediment runoff have impacted the raw water source and caused a decline in water quality and water quantity. Overall, this project will ensure that this small, rural town will have the needed funds to install new equipment and replace damaged intake infrastructure which will contribute to the improvement of the communitys water system for years to come.

naics_national_industry: OFFICES OF PHYSICIANS, MENTAL HEALTH SPECIALISTS
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide Emergency Rural Health Care Grant funds to South Lane Mental Health (SLMH), located in rural Cottage Grove, Oregon. This is a follow-on award to a previous award of $58,200 due to increased expenses. The project includes air purifiers; gazebo and outdoor furniture; heating; ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) installation; and key fobs. This facility presently does not have air filtration systems, outdoor meeting spaces or secure entry systems. An improved HVAC system is needed to improve air quality at the main SLMH facility. These improvements will reduce the impact and spread of COVID-19 by allowing for safer meeting spaces, healthier air quality in offices, and more secure and selective entry to facilities to screen for symptoms. Overall, the subsequent funding for this project will ensure that this vital facility continues to provide services to residents of the surrounding communities for years to come.

funding_code: CF ARP EMERGENCY RURAL HEALTH CARE GRANTS - TRACK 1 & 2
naics_industry_sector: Health Care and Social Assistance
naics_national_industry: OFFICES OF PHYSICIANS, MENTAL HEALTH SPECIALISTS
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase a covered gazebo, picnic tables and chairs to facilitate outdoor COVID safe therapy sessions, HEPA air purifiers for offices to further protect clients and clinicians and a new key fob system to increase security and the ability to screen visitors for COVID. South Lane Mental Health has several care facilities in the community of Cottage Grove. These facilities do not currently have an air filtration system or outdoor meeting areas. These improvements are needed to reduce the impact and spread of COVID by allowing for safer meeting spaces, healthier air quality in offices and the ability to more safely screen for symptoms upon entry into the facilities. Overall, this project will ensure that this rural area will have the needed funds to purchase equipment and enhance its capabilities to respond to COVID for the residents of Cottage Grove and the surrounding area for years to come.

funding_code: CF ARP EMERGENCY RURAL HEALTH CARE GRANTS - TRACK 1 & 2
naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help fund increased staffing costs related to the COVID pandemic for the Florence Food Share, a nonprofit emergency food box pantry located in the rural town of Florence, Oregon. The Food Shares mission is to alleviate hunger in Western Lane County. They serve approximately 1,700 low income and needy families every month, also serve the coastal communities from Yachats to Gardiner and inland to Mapleton. Florence Food Share are regarded as an important food provider in the area, and this project will ensure that this vital facility in the heart of a small, rural town of Florence continues to provide emergency food supplies to residents of the surrounding area for years to come.

funding_code: CF GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Other or Not Defined
naics_national_industry: OTHER FIRE/RESCUE & PUBLIC SAFETY RELATED SERVICES
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide sub-funding to assist with the purchase of communications repeater equipment for the rural town of Florence, Oregon. The repeater allows for radio communications from law enforcement officers and other first responders throughout the citys service area. Sub-funding is needed due to increase in cost of equipment. The citys existing communications repeater is located at its communications tower on Hermans Peak in unincorporated Lane County, outside the citys limits. The city shares the tower with the Western Lane Ambulance District and the Siuslaw Valley Rescue and Fire District. The current equipment mounted on the tower has reached its useful life and is in need of replacement. The city is partnering with the Oregon Department of Transportation (ODOT) on the project, and ODOT has agreed to provide an upgraded system; however, the repeater that the city must purchase in order to connect to the upgraded system is more costly than the originally approved one. For this reason, the project budget increased and additional grant funds are needed in order to complete the project. Overall, this project will ensure that this vital equipment in the small, rural town of Florence will continue to provide this vital public service for years to come.

project_name: Water Treatment Filters and Pump Station Improvements
funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) ECWAG - APPROPRIATED $1,000,000 LIMIT
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide funds to the rural city of Gates, Oregon to install the following: a backup power source at their reservoir, a grid-connected solar cell and battery onsite, forty-four replacement water filter modules, a steel mesh net wall to maintain road access, and a new Thistledown Booster Pump Station. The city of Gates, located 35 miles east of Salem, sustained major damage during the September 2020 wildfires. Roughly 50 percent of the homes and structures in the city were destroyed, resulting in exposed service lines and massive system leaks. This caused the reservoir to run dry, as the reservoir lacks backup power. In addition, the citys water intake has shown increased turbidity during the subsequent rainy seasons. The filters are unable to treat water this contaminated. If a steep, burned embankment fails, the water treatment plant will become inaccessible. Additionally, the Thistledown Booster Pump Station ran without water for an extended period causing damage and must be replaced to prevent future disruption of service. Overall, this project will ensure that the water facility in the heart of Gates, Oregon continues to provide vital services to the community for years to come.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to to develop a Wasco County electric vehicle (EV) charging plan. funding_code: CF ARP EMERGENCY RURAL HEALTH CARE GRANTS - TRACK 1 & 2
naics_industry_sector: Other or Not Defined
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help purchase equipment to start a tele pharmacy and enhance capabilities to respond to COVID-19. The residents of Elgin have been without a pharmacy for 15 years and must drive into La Grande, 20 miles away to get their prescriptions. The Elgin Health District built the clinic in 2008 and currently offers medical, dental and limited behavioral health services in rural Elgin, but it has no pharmacy. The health care clinic will purchase and install tele pharmacy equipment at the clinic location and at Grande Ronde Hospital in La Grande. This project will ensure that this rural area will have the needed funds to purchase tele pharmacy equipment and enhance its capabilities to provide enhanced medical services to the residents of Elgin and the surrounding area for years to come.

funding_code: CF ARP EMERGENCY RURAL HEALTH CARE GRANTS - TRACK 1 & 2
naics_industry_sector: Wholesale Trade
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help purchase equipment which will enhance the capability to respond to COVID 19. The Grande Ronde Hospital is a non-profit 25-bed critical access hospital located in La Grande, Oregon and serves all of Union County. The Grande Ronde Hospital will purchase and install negative air pressure equipment for the pediatric unit, a BioFire PCR analyzer for COVID 19 testing and two electronic reader board signs to provide COVID 19 related information at the hospital and the urgent care clinic. Overall, this project will ensure that this rural area will have the needed funds to purchase hospital equipment and enhance its capabilities to respond to COVID 19 by providing enhanced medical services to the residents of La Grande and the entire county for years to come.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to assist a small farm in Clackamas County. Jennifer Van Wey dba Quackenbush Farm, is a mixed vegetable farm located in Eagle Creek, Oregon. This project will create one new job.

funding_code: REAP-MAND ENERGY EFF IMPROV GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Retail Trade
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help Space Industries, a design and manufacturing small business focused on celebrating science in Redmond, Oregon, purchase and install a complete overhaul of the buildings lighting which will include transitioning every bulb and fixture from incandescent/fluorescent to LED. A total of 215 fixtures will be removed and replaced with 191 energy-efficient fixtures. This upgrade is projected to save an average of 55,756 kilowatt hours per year. In addition, there will an installation of an insulated dividing wall in the warehouse to allow for zonal heating. The wall will drop the total heated area of the warehouse down to less than a third of the current square footage. This will allow the manufacturing and pick/pack area to be maintained at a comfortable working temperature while allowing deep storage to be maintained at freeze-protection to conserve energy. Lastly, there will be an upgraded HVAC control units for the office space that will prevent simultaneous heating and cooling (currently the only setting available) and allow for more efficient control of the climate in each office and space, along with upgraded controllers in the warehouse space will allow for additional energy savings through more accurate zonal venting and better control of the heaters. These upgrades will save Space Industries LLC $11,619 per year in energy costs.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to expand a health center in the rural city of Roseburg in southwest Ore. Overall, this project will create 20 jobs and save an additional 60 jobs in rural southwest Oregon.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to fund emergency improvements to the Dexter Oaks Cooperatives two wells, which serves a community of 88 people in the unincorporated community of Dexter in rural Lane County. Unfortunately, current drought conditions have resulted in the drop in water quality in one well and higher concentrations of arsenic in the other. The Dexter Oaks Cooperative Board have been purchasing jugs of water and distributing them to residents for drinking and cooking as a short term stopgap measure (reimbursement for the purchase of emergency water is included in the project cost). For the long term solution, funding will cover the cost of abandonment of Well #1 (which will be replaced by drilling a new well). Additionally, a 35,000-gallon reservoir, new control building, and backup arsenic treatment will be included in the upgraded water system. Once completed, this project will ensure that the Dexter Oaks Cooperative will continue to provide a vital service to the community for years to come.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will provide additional financing to A4 Quality Property LLC to purchase a turn-key Travel Centers of America truck stop with afast food restaurant and convenience store in the rural eastern Oregon town ofHuntington, located in Malheur County. The project is used as a fueling station and convenience store with both hot-and-ready and grab-and-go food geared toward the trucking industry and general public. The facility is located along I-84 at Hwy 30, with I-84 being Oregon & Washingtons primary East-West route with Idaho, Utah and beyond. The travel center sits about 30 miles from the Idaho border and is about 85 miles west of Boise, Idaho and 138 miles southeast of Pendleton, Oregon. One of the main reasons the site was chosen is that it shares the highway exit with an Oregon-State weigh station where commercial trucks are required to stop. This highway exit also serves as the gateway to a large regional park where travelers visit to stretch their legs, let their dogs out, etc, The Huntington Travel Center of America is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week and has very good visibility from I-84 and Hwy 30 with electronic signage at the highway, providing a much needed service to rural Oregon travelers.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help a remote lodge in the Eagle Cap Wilderness in northeast Oregon expand its renewable energy system. Minam River Lodge will use the USDA grant to purchase and install solar panels to expand its solar energy system. The additional solar panels will produce 13,693 kilowatt-hours of renewable electricity per year, which is enough to power one typical U.S. home. The new solar panels will offset the diesel generator currently used to provide energy for the lodge, saving not only the cost of the fuel but also the cost of flying the fuel, six drums at a time, to this remote location in the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest because it is not accessible by road. The expanded renewable energy system will reduce the energy costs of this unique wilderness lodge by $16,321 per year.

funding_code: RBCS ENTERPRISE GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Other or Not Defined
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to develop small and emerging businesses in Benton County in western Ore. The rural community of Philomath will use the USDA grant to implement the Linn-Benton Collaborative using an already proven entrepreneur development program offered by the nonprofit Oregon Regional Accelerator and Innovation Network (Oregon RAIN). The collaborative will help build an entrepreneurial ecosystem and economy in the region by providing technical assistance to local entrepreneurs. Oregon RAIN will provide entrepreneurs with workshops, pre-launch business development, seminars and training, a mentoring program, referrals, and financial resources. In addition, the nonprofit will host a "pitch-fest" featuring start-ups introducing its business concepts. In the first year, this project will culminate in a user survey and case study, with the intention of continuing the program in subsequent years.

funding_code: REAP-MANDATORY RENEW ENERGY SYST GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help a farm in northwest Ore. develop a renewable energy system. Kenagy Family Farm outside the rural town Albany will use the USDA grant to purchase and install a 46-kilowatt solar array on the roof of its barn. This system will generate an estimated 49,090 kilowatt-hours of renewable electricity per year, which is enough to power five typical U.S. homes. The solar array will replace 19 percent of the farms energy use, saving Kenagy Family Farm $5,168 per year through the reduction of its utility bill and income from the the sale of renewable energy back to the grid.

funding_code: DISCRETION ASSIST MICROPENTERPRENUERS
naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This USDA Rural Development investment will be used by the nonprofit Oregon Cascades West Council of Governments (OCWCOG) to increase access to capital for small businesses in the rural areas surrounding the town of Albany in western Oregon. With this USDA grant, OCWCOG will increase the financing available through its rural microloan revolving fund, which provides vital financial support to small businesses in Linn County. This project will help foster an environment of entrepreneurship by giving business owners the technical assistance they need to create jobs, expand operations, enter into new markets, and fuel the local economy.

naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable the Henry Estate Winery in southwest Oregon to expand its retail and direct-to-customer wine sales. The Henry Estate Winery produces fine, hand-crafted wines from many grape varietals grown on its estate in the rural community of Umqua. The winery will use its USDA grant to implement a digital marketing and retail sale event campaign. The winery will also strive to increase its wine club membership throughout the United States, with an emphasis on the West Coast. Overall, this value-added agriculture project will increase the customer base for this winery while enabling it to retain three jobs and creating one additional job in this very small, rural community of 112 people.

funding_code: CF 2019 DISASTER GRANT - TORNADOES FLOODS OTHER
naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase and upfit a Ford Police Interceptor SUV for the police department of Reedsport. This city is located along the Oregon coast in western Douglas County. The Reedsport Police Department is the only law enforcement in the county and is routinely called upon to respond to calls outside of the city in partnership with Oregon State Police and Douglas County Sheriffs Office. The department currently has five older Ford police vehicles in their fleet with over 115,000 miles on them. Ford has discontinued these models and no longer makes many of the parts necessary for repairs, making maintenance costly and potentially impossible. The new vehicle, complete with upfitting for police equipment, will allow the department to retire one of these older vehicles and keep it on-hand for spare parts. This will allow the department to continue serving and protecting their rural community, along with the surrounding area for years to come.

funding_code: CF 2019 DISASTER GRANT - TORNADOES FLOODS OTHER
naics_industry_sector: Public Administration
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to update the law enforcement department facilities in the rural town of Winston in southwest Ore. The public parking lot in front of the Winston Law Enforcement buildings deteriorating, while the department uses a field behind the building for employee and patrol officers vehicle parking. Neither area is in compliance with updated Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards. The town of Winston will use this grant to pave both parking lots, stripe both lots, install sidewalks, and construct access ramps that meet ADA requirements. Overall, this project will improve access to the department for the residents of this rural community while enabling the department to better protect its investment in its vehicles, ensuring the community has access to public safety services for years to come.

funding_code: RBCS ENTERPRISE GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Other Services
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to develop small and emerging businesses in Grant County in central Ore. Grant County will use the USDA grant to implement the Startup Grant County initiative using an already proven entrepreneur development program offered by the nonprofit Oregon Regional Accelerator and Innovation Network (Oregon RAIN). This initiative will help build an entrepreneurial ecosystem and economy in the region. Oregon RAIN will provide workshops, one-on-one mentoring, and help developing and updating business plans for local entrepreneurs. In addition, this project will help startups and small businesses weather the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic by connecting Grant County entrepreneurs to a network of experts and programming to help them rework its finances, improve its outreach, connect them to emergency funding sources, and help them complete applications. Overall, this project will create seven jobs and enable local businesses to retain 15 jobs in this rural county while helping businesses get started, grow, and survive the pandemic and economic crisis.

This project will reduce the motels energy bill by $22,800 per year.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to expand a hotel in the rural town of Hood River in northern Oregon. The family-owned-and-operated Westcliff Lodge opened in 1954 and currently offers 57 guest rooms. However, to keep pace with demand, the hotel needs to expand. The project will enable the construction of an additional building with another 36 guest rooms that include all furnishings, fixtures, and equipment, as well as a maintenance office. funding_code: RBCS ENTERPRISE GRANTS
naics_industry_sector: Other Services
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to improve the viability of Latino businesses in the Mid-Columbia Gorge region in northern Ore. The nonprofit The Next Door will use this USDA grant to help create economic opportunity for Latinos through its Programa Promoviendo Prosperidad (Promoting Prosperity Program or PPP). The program will help Latinos build sustainable small businesses and increase its financial stability. The nonprofit will provide technical assistance and support to Latino small business owners and aspiring entrepreneurs, including assistance with business registration, health department permits, and other licenses; financial literacy; and access to capital. Overall, this project will create 1 full-time and 10 part-time jobs while also helping local businesses retain 85 full-time and 55 part-time jobs in the small, rural towns of the Columbia River Gorge.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help a museum in the rural town of Ashland in southwest Oregon develop a renewable energy system. The USDA grant will be used to purchase and install a 35-kilowatt solar array with a dual axis tracker in the parking lot of the ScienceWorks Hands-on Museum. As the third phase of the museums renewable energy project, this ground-mounted system will produce enough renewable electricity to power 10 typical U.S. homes. This project will generate $9,158 per year for the museum through the sale of the renewable electricity back to the grid.

naics_industry_sector: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to help a rural business in the town of Ashland in southwest Oregon develop a renewable energy system. Ashland Automotive, a locally-owned business, will use the USDA grant to purchase and install an 83.3-kilowatt solar array. This system will generate an estimated 131,042 kilowatt-hours of renewable electricity per year, which is enough to power 16 typical U.S. homes. Overall, the solar array will help this small, rural business save $13,104 per year using virtual net metering.

project_name: VAPG FY20 WC FOR YAK MEAT
funding_code: VALUE-ADDED PRODUCER DVLP GRANTS-DISCR
naics_industry_sector: Wholesale Trade
naics_national_industry: MEAT AND MEAT PRODUCT MERCHANT WHOLESALERS
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable Firebird Farms in southwest Oregon to expand its sale of artisan yak charcuterie. Firebird Farms is a woman-owned business that raises a 60-head yak herd outside the rural town of Ashland. It produces breeding stock, fiber, dairy, and meat, including hand-crafted jerky, smoked sausage, cured meats, and salami, which command a higher price then more traditional meat cuts. The farm will use its USDA grant to implement a strategic marketing strategy that incorporates retail sale events to expand its direct sale of grass-fed yak meat and artisan chacuterie from Ashland to the greater Rogue Valley. Overall, this value-added agriculture project will expand the sale of specialty yak meats while enabling Firebird Farms to retain one job and create an additional job in this rural community.

funding_code: VALUE-ADDED PRODUCER DVLP GRANTS-DISCR
naics_industry_sector: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable Uproot Meats in southwest Oregon to expand its meat production and customer base. Uproot Meat is a woman-owned business in the rural town of Ashland that produces locally-sourced, ethically-raised pork and chicken. It butchers the meat and sells it to local retailers, select restaurants, and directly to customers through a CSA. Uproot Meats will use its USDA grant to increase production and implement a strategic marketing initiative that incorporates retail events. Overall, this value-added agriculture project will expand the farms sale of sustainably farmed, nutrient-dense meat and create two additional jobs in this rural community.

funding_code: VALUE-ADDED PRODUCER DVLP GRANTS-DISCR
naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable B&B Organics in southwest Oregon to expand its wine production, marketing, and sales. B&B Organics is a certified biodynamic farm and winery in the rural town of Jacksonville. Its Cowhorn wines are made with premium Rh ne grapes and require high profit margins. B&B Organics will use the USDA grant to market the wine in large metropolitan areas such as Seattle, Washington; Portland, Oregon; Richmond, Virginia; and Napa, California. Overall, this value-added project will increase the sale of the vineyards organic wine and create four additional jobs in this rural town.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable Whistling Duck Farm in southwest Oregon to increase its marketing of fermented vegetable products. Whistling Duck Farm is a certified organic vegetable farm in the rural town of Grants Pass. It creates farm-fresh fermented vegetables, including krauts, kimchi, pickles, relishes, tapenades, pastes, beet kvass, and brine-based fresh dressings. The farm will use its USDA grant to implement strategic marketing initiatives and increase the sale of these products through wholesale, direct-to-customer, farmers market, restaurant, and retailer sales. Overall, this value-added agriculture project will expand the sale of the farms organic fermented vegetable products and create three jobs in this rural town.

project_name: VAPG FY20 WC FOR HARD CIDER
funding_code: VALUE-ADDED PRODUCER DVLP GRANTS-DISCR
naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable Thompson Creek Organics in southwest Oregon to produce and market a new hard cider. Thompson Creek Organics is an organic apple orchard in the rural town of Applegate that produces sweet non-alcoholic ciders and a line of hard ciders, Apple Outlaw Cider. The orchard will use its USDA grant to develop its new Imperial Cider using different fermentation and aging techniques to adapt to changing trends in the cider market. The farm will also develop an orchard retail outlet where local customers can taste and purchase cider, learn about the orchards operations, take a tour, and pick apples. Overall, this value-added agriculture project will enable Thompson Creek Organics to develop a new organic cider, educate local customers about the cider creation process, and retain three jobs while also creating an additional job in this small, rural community.

naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable Territorial Vineyards and Wine Company in southwest Oregon to expand its wine production and wholesale distribution. Territorial Vineyards and Wine Company in Eugene is a sustainable, dry-farmed estate vineyard that has created carefully-crafted wines from its custom, low yield, high quality grapes. Territorial will use its USDA grant to increase production by hiring an assistant winemaker and a cellar hand. It will also implement strategic marketing initiatives to increase its sales in the wholesale market. Overall, this value-added agriculture project will expand the production and sale of the vineyards wines while retaining four jobs and creating an additional two jobs in this rural area.

funding_code: VALUE-ADDED PRODUCER DVLP GRANTS-DISCR
naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable Iris Vineyards in southwest Oregon to expand its sale of sustainably produced wine. Iris Vineyards dry farms Pinot Gris, Chardonnay, and Pinot Noir vines outside the rural town of Cottage Grove. The vineyard will use its USDA grant to expand the production, marketing, and sale of its wines. It will market to commercial distribution retailers such as Costco, small wine shops, and restaurants. The vineyard will also strive to increase its wine club memberships throughout the United States, with an emphasis on the West Coast. Overall, this value-added agriculture project will expand the sale of Iris Vineyards sustainably produced wine while enabling it to retain seven jobs and create an additional two positions in this rural community.

funding_code: VALUE-ADDED PRODUCER DVLP GRANTS-DISCR
naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable Deck Family Farm in southwest Oregon to expand its marketing and sale of pasture-raised poultry. Deck Family Farm in the rural town of Junction City uses regenerative agriculture practices to raise poultry for the local food industry in a sustainable manner. The farm will use its USDA grant to expand its marketing of packaged poultry to increase its direct-to-customer sales and wholesale distribution. Deck Family Farm will hire a marketing director to manage all aspects of branding, customer outreach, and direct marketing to targeted retail customers through promotional events. Overall, this value-added agriculture project will enable Deck Family Farm increase its sale of sustainably-raised poultry while creating an additional three jobs in this rural community.

funding_code: RCDI RURAL COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVE GRANT
naics_industry_sector: Other or Not Defined
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to fuel economic recovery by building the capacity of community main street organizations. Rural Development Initiatives will establish a program to equip main street organizations to serve key functions in the local business support ecosystem by giving them greater resources and support, building more productive relationships among businesses, and helping the communities implement economic vitality initiatives in their downtown regions. The program will span multiple states, and the USDA funding will be used to assist communities in Klamath, Union, Umatilla, and Malheur counties in Ore., as well as Skamania County in Wash. Overall, this project will help five rural communities in Ore. and southern Wash. increase economic vitality and recover from the economic crisis by supporting business retention and growth, increasing the diversity of businesses, and strengthening business clusters.

funding_code: CF 2019 DISASTER GRANT - TORNADOES FLOODS OTHER
naics_industry_sector: Educational Services
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to construct an emergency shelter for the City of Oakridge. The communitys designated Red Cross shelter, Oakridge High School, does not have an appropriate space to be used as a shelter, nor a dedicated emergency generator to provide power. A 2019 snowstorm forced residents and local volunteers to sleep in hallways and classrooms of the high school while seeking shelter. This project will renovate unused space in the athletic facility into an 8,500 square foot multipurpose room that can serve as a shelter during emergencies, such as snowstorms or wildfires, and also increase the functionality of the athletic program. The project will also install a permanent emergency generator, allowing the school to safely function as a shelter and also continue classes during regular power outages. When completed, this project will provide this rural community with a designated shelter that will allow the school to remain open for classes while providing shelter for evacuees. It will also be a useful space for the school during the rest of the school year for community meetings and other educational and after school activities.

project_name: Beaver Creek Water Source Project-Phase IV
funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide additional financing for increased construction cost. Currently, the Seal Rock Water District receives treated drinking water from the town of Toledo. This water source is vulnerable to failure as a result of storms and earth movement. The treated water travels approximately 10 miles from Toledo through a dedicated transmission pipe that passes through tsunami inundation zones and areas prone to landslides and flooding. In the event of a natural disaster, the line is difficult to access and repair. In recent years, the system has failed several times, requiring costly emergency responses to restore service. In the event of Cascadia Subduction Zone earthquake, the water source is expected to collapse. Recent studies found that the most favorable solution is to develop the districts own primary water supply from Beaver Creek, for which the district received water withdrawal authorization in 2016. The funding from USDA will be used to construct a treatment plant that uses membrane filtration to clean the water, install a water pipeline, build a 500,000-gallon reservoir, install submersible pumps in Beaver Creek, and install backup power generators. The treatment plant will be located on district-owned property above the tsunami impact zone. The facilities will be designed to take Oregons Resiliency Plan into consideration, which includes rapid recovery measures. This municipal water project will provide the district with a reliable water source and infrastructure that is built to new seismic and tsunami resiliency standards while addressing the states rapid recovery goals, ensuring safe drinking water for this rural community of 4,340 people.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable the Tillamook County Creamery Association to expand the sale of its cheese and ice cream products into the Singapore market. The tribal-run nonprofit ONABEN will use this USDA grant to implement the training program Journey: Expanding the Landscape of Native Entrepreneurs. This program will provide business development training in rural, underserved Native communities, including Harney, Polk, and Umatilla counties in Ore.; Cherokee, Sequoyah, McCurtain, McIntosh, and Tulsa counties in Okla.; and the Eastern Band of Cherokee community in N.C.s Swain County. project_announced_description: Rural Development funds will be used by the Manufactured Housing Cooperative Development (MHCD) Center operated by the housing nonprofit Community and Shelter Assistance Corporation (CASA) to support resident-owned manufactured housing communities. The nonprofit will provide technical assistance to facilitate the conversion of manufactured housing parks to residential ownership and to support the long-term success of the new cooperatives. These cooperatives will empower residents to improve site management, address facility upgrade needs, and preserve and enhance access to safe, affordable housing, which will help stabilize the overall community. The grant funds will also support a feasibility study of future opportunities to form new manufactured housing cooperatives. Overall, 12 manufactured housing communities throughout rural Oregon will receive assistance with adopting a cooperative structure.

funding_code: VALUE-ADDED PRODUCER DVLP GRANTS-DISCR
naics_industry_sector: Manufacturing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide working capital to enable Sokol Blosser Winery in northwest Oregon to expand its customer base. Sokol Blosser Winery in the rural town of Dayton creates organic, sustainably-crafted wines. The winery will use its USDA grant to implement a strategic digital marketing campaign and to conduct retail sales events to increase its direct-to-customer and national sales. The winery will also strive to increase its tasting room visitor-ship and on-site sale of its estate-grown wine. Overall, this value-added agriculture project will increase Sokol Blosser Winerys customer base and sale of organic, sustainably-produced wines.

funding_code: RRH-NONSUBSIDIZED-SEC538 GUARANTEED
naics_industry_sector: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase and retrofit an affordable apartment complex in the rural town of McMinnville in northwest Ore. and to maintain affordable rates for low-income residents. The rehabilitation will include a renovation of the exterior of Glenhaven Park McMinnville, from new roofing and siding, a repaved parking lot, new concrete walkways, the installation of exterior pole lights, trash enclosures, new landscaping, replacement of gutters, and new exterior paint. The interior of the apartment complex will also be thoroughly remodeled by replacing windows, doors, insulation, cabinets, flooring, lights, and appliances, as well as fully updating kitchens and bathrooms. The renovation will include accessibility improvements such as parking spaces and ramps throughout the complex. Finally, building safety will be improved with new fire extinguishers, smoke detectors, and door locks. Overall, this project will preserve 36 units of affordable rental housing, along with the rental assistance provided by USDA for 28 low-income families at this apartment to help ensure they pay no more than 30 percent of their income on housing.

funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) ECWAG - APPROPRIATED $1,000,000 LIMIT
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This USDA Rural Development investment will be used by the rural town of Prairie City in eastern Oregon to make water system improvements that will help the community maintain adequate utility services despite increasingly frequent drought conditions. Prairie Citys municipal water system serves 410 users in this rural community, which is designated as a distressed area by the State of Oregon. Prairie City will make improvements to its municipal water system. A pump station and water transmission line will be installed, connecting a previously unused well to the communitys main water transmission line. Additionally, a power line will be installed leading to the pump station, and the access road will be updated. Additional funding is being provided by the state agency Business Oregon in the amount of $727,000. Overall, these improvements will increase water production for this rural community of 909 people, ensuring continued access to drinking water and a sufficient water supply to respond to fires during future droughts.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to scale up an entrepreneur development program and improve business development in the rural community of Florence on the Oregon coast. The town of Florence will use this project to contract with the nonprofit Regional Accelerator and Innovation Network of Oregon, known as Oregon RAIN, to scale up a proven entrepreneur development program. This venture catalyst program provides technical assistance and training for start-ups, as well as existing and expanding businesses in search of funding opportunities. The Rural Entrepreneurial Development Model provides workshops, face-to-face meetings with individual entrepreneurs, coaching, and access to training, funding, and other resources. Overall, this project will help businesses in this rural community get off the ground or expand and is expected to create 25 jobs.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to create a new city hall for the rural town of Yachats on the Ore. coast. The Yachats City Hall is located in a 1930-era building that was used as a schoolhouse until the 1980s. Today, the building houses city hall, an after-school and daycare center, council chambers, and space for community activities and private rentals. The city hall space can no longer meet the needs of the community. The reception area is small. The office lacks dedicated space for the city manager, and the other staff share a cramped workspace. The USDA grant will be used to renovate a neighboring building for use as city hall. The new building has sufficient space, meets Americans with Disabilities Act accessibility standards, and offers plenty of parking for public meetings. The renovations will include adding a reception area and delineating council chambers, the sheriffs deputy office, and workspace for other staff.

project_announced_description: This USDA Rural Development investment will be used to retrofit an affordable apartment complex for farmworkers and their families in the rural town of Milton-Freewater in northeast Oregon. The exterior of Orchard Homes will be completely renovated by installing new siding, replacing the roof, repaving the parking lot, installing concrete walkways and pole lights, building trash enclosures, updating the landscaping, replacing the gutters, and painting the buildings. The interior of the apartment complex will also be thoroughly remodeled by replacing windows, doors, insulation, cabinets, flooring, lights, and appliances, as well as fully updating kitchens and bathrooms. The renovation will include accessibility improvements, such as adding handicap parking spaces and ramps throughout the complex. Finally, building safety will be improved with new fire extinguishers, smoke detectors, and door locks. Overall, this renovation project will preserve 127 units of affordable rental housing for farm workers in this small, rural community, along with USDA rental assistance for qualified low-income families living at the apartment complex.
